# LangSlice

:::{container} ls-lead
Give LangSlice a folder of brain-section images. An AI agent places each
section in a brain atlas and draws the atlas region borders on it. You can
then assign cells and signal to brain regions.
:::

:::{admonition} Before you start
:class: important

- **Your AI provider sees your sections.** Pictures of them go to OpenAI,
  Google or Anthropic, whichever runs your app, and a registration counts
  against your plan's usage limits. Your image files stay on your computer,
  unchanged.
- **Check every result.** The agent can be wrong.
:::

:::{admonition} In development
:class: warning

The LangSlice window (the agent viewer, the prompt generator and Settings) is
new and still changing. Registration runs without it.
:::

**New here?** Start with [Installation](getting-started/install.md).

## Cite LangSlice

Baughman, N. (2026). *LangSlice: VLM-driven registration of histological brain
sections to BrainGlobe atlases* (version 0.2.1) [Computer software]. Zenodo.
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23900540>

That DOI stands for every version; [Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23900540)
lists a DOI for each release, to cite the exact one you used.

GitHub's **Cite this repository** button gives it as BibTeX. Questions and
problems go to [GitHub issues](https://github.com/greenpolo/LangSlice/issues).
